- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or align with 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.1) and price drops, model underestimates the fall; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply a 1–3% downward bias for first 7 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day window; if forecast is >10% above 10-day MA, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model ignores sentiment; force a 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment to reflect sentiment decay.
